newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul exchange details stock index options rules.
newsitem.headline: Seoul exchange details stock index options rules.

text.p: South Korea's stock exchange said on Friday it would not limit price fluctuations in stock-index options trading, which is set to start from July 7.
The Korea Stock Exchange has finalised a set of rules on options trading, which would be submitted to the Ministry of Finance and Economy for approval.
Sixty products would be offered, the exchange said.
The exchange said it had adopted a European-style options market, where options can be exercised only on the last trading day, which is the second Thursday of each expiration month.

Investors would be able to buy products that expire within the next three consecutive months and three of the months of March, June, September and December, which are not included in the three consecutive months.
The market will have two types of options -- KOSPI 200 call option and KOSPI 200 put option, the exchange said.
The size of a contract was set at 100,000 won.
Trading hours would be 9 to 11:30 a.m. (0000-0230 GMT) and 1 to 3:15 p.m. (0400 to 0615 GMT).
On the last trading day, the afternoon session would run from 1 to 2:50 p.m. (0400 to 0550 GMT). Half-day trading sessions would run from 9:30 to 11:45 a.m. (0030 to 0245 GMT).
The exchange estimated the options trading volume would reach 205 trillion won in 2000, compared with 192 trillion won estimated for spot stock trading.
